title: Hitching a ride to Chicago in 1933
summary: After a woman problem, he talks a Kansas City club owner into driving him to Chicago, then reflects on helping others.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: But in 1933 I had a problem with a woman. So, I was so angry 'til I went out on the highway with my bags and this man that owned the Cherry Blossom came past...he was just going for a drive and he saw me and say, "where you going?" I say, "well, I'm going as far as you go." And do you know that I convinced that man, in Kansas City, to drive me to St. Louis at eight o'clock in the morning. I convinced that man, Dan, to drive me from St. Louis to 39th Street and South Parkway by the Grand Terrace. Now that's pretty good talking. And he did it and I guess he was glad, he was proud of it. Well, I guess he was so fascinated...I was telling him so many yarns about how great he was, and what he should do is to go to Chicago because there are a lot of chorus girls and pretty women and they'd come back to Kansas City with him, you know, without any hesitation whatsoever, and he went for it. He went for it, you know. And I was so embarassed...I went in one door in this
hotel next to the Grand Terrace...I went in one door and out the other.

I still remember how nice he was to me and I think this is what make me, you know, kind to people. If I see a person on the highway, if I can help, or...well, actually, I believe, though, that this kind of feeling that I have for helping people became more when my wife became ill, because after having a four year experience with my wife being ill from '74 to '78, then I had, you know, I created that soft spot in my heart... it really came to the fore. And I just really...I'm an old man myself, but I help old people across the street now that are probably younger than I am. Today no day will pass that I won't try to help a person. You know, I go out of my way to do it. In many instances I says, "How old are you, dear?" and she says, "61." I say, "Oh, gee, I got you by ten years." (laughter). But I say, somebody should be helping me across the street and here I am, the Good Samaritan.
